tip: Bare να (na) + verb gives friendly advice: να πας (na pas = you should go) – no 'should' word needed, the να carries it.
Greek usually drops subject pronouns, so adding one marks contrast: εμείς πήραμε σαλάτα (emís pírame saláta = we ordered salad) – εμείς stresses whose order it was.
Present tense + τώρα = have been: περιμένουμε... τώρα (periménume... tóra = we've been waiting).
Λείπει ένα πιρούνι (lípi éna pirúni = a fork is missing) – λείπει covers absent people too: λείπει ο Νίκος (lípi o Níkos = Nikos is away).
Πόδι (pódi) covers both foot and leg: το πόδι του τραπεζιού (to pódi tu trapeziú = the table leg). Greek uses one word for the whole limb.
Clock times are normally plural: στις έντεκα (stis éndeka = at eleven) – the feminine plural στις agrees with the unspoken ώρες (óres = hours).
Έμεινε λίγο φαγητό (émine lígho fayitó = there's some food left) – μένω (méno) also means to stay.
Στο πόδι (sto pódi = on the go, lit. on the foot) – eating standing up.
Μάς έκανε τραπέζι (mas ékane trapézi = treated us to a meal, lit. made us a table) – κάνω τραπέζι (káno trapézi) is the standard invite-to-dinner idiom.
Personal names normally take the article: κι ο Γιώργος (ki o Yórgos = Giorgos too) – Greek says the Giorgos, dropping ο mainly when speaking to him directly.
Μετρό never changes form: του μετρό (tu metró = of the metro) – borrowed words like this usually stay the same everywhere.
Πόσο κάνει; (póso káni) = how much is it? – the everyday way to ask prices.
Χτυπάω την κάρτα (khtipáo tin kárta) = tap the card – χτυπάω also means knock and ring.
Πρέπει να (prépi na) = have to, must – πρέπει stays the same for every person, and the verb after it changes instead.
Κατεβαίνω (katevéno) = I get off – literally 'I go down'.
Η γραμμή (i gramí) = line – metro and phone lines; a queue of people is η ουρά (i urá).
Αλλάζω γραμμή (alázo gramí) = I change lines – no article needed before γραμμή.
Περνάει (pernái) = it passes, comes by – buses, time and pain all περνάνε (pernáne).
Χάνω (kháno) = lose and miss: χάσαμε το λεωφορείο (khásame to leoforío) = we missed the bus.
Με + transport = by: με ταξί (me taxí) = by taxi.
Time phrases normally take the article: τη νύχτα (ti níkhta) = at night.
Μέχρι (mékhri) = until, as far as: μέχρι το λιμάνι (mékhri to limáni) = as far as the port.
Αφήνω (afíno) = leave, let: με αφήνετε εδώ; (me afínete edhó) = will you drop me here?
Greeks usually ask directions with the future: πώς θα πάω; (pos tha páo) = how do I get there?
Directions usually come in the you-form: πας... στρίβεις (pas... strívis) = you go... you turn.
Δεν βρίσκω (dhen vrísko) = I can't find – Greek just says 'I don't find'.
ΚΤΕΛ (KTEL) = Greece's intercity buses – every region has its own.
Κρατάω (kratáo) = hold, but with a stretch of time it means last: κράτησε (krátise) = it lasted.
Greek arrives 'with delay': με δύο ώρες καθυστέρηση (me dhío óres kathistérisi = with two hours' delay) is the standard way to say 'two hours late'.
Weather takes έχει (ékhi = it has): έχει πολύ αέρα (ékhi polí aéra) = it's very windy.
